text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: production-inference error-rate spike (503/502) — automatic page to oncall at 1898765432. Affected service: runtime-frontend. Docs: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prod-inference

Sam (oncall): Got it, joining bridge. Initial graphs show errors up ~42% starting ~1898765400. I'm opening a bridge.

Alice Chen: On it — I'm seeing a surge of 502s from `runtime-frontend` -> `inference-worker` with 5xx traces mentioning `kv-cache` failures. Pushing logs into thread.

Miguel Ramos: Reproduced in staging? No, staging fine. Prod only and only in us-west-2.

Priya Singh: Customer impact: telemetry shows increased latency + failed requests, ~4 customers >5% failure on realtime endpoints. Not yet hitting billing/regulatory customers list.

Liz Eng: Sharing log snippet from runtime-frontend (redacted):
```
[2026-03-15T18:10:02Z] worker=inf-23 status=502 upstream_error="KV cache miss, eviction error: device OOM" pid=2231
[2026-03-15T18:10:02Z] stack=\"runtime/kernel_dispatch() -> kv_cache_retrieve() -> cudaMalloc() failed: out of memory\"
```

Sam (oncall): Good. Hypothesis 1: KV cache eviction causing OOM on GPU, leading to worker failures and 502s. Hypothesis 2: recent kernel runtime patch (rolled 2h ago) has changed allocation behavior.

Alice Chen: FYI we rolled `inference-kernel v3.4.2` at 16:05 (automated canary -> roll). I'll check rollout window against host crashes.

Miguel Ramos: Metrics: GPU memory pressure on that pool increased from 68% -> 96% between 16:02-18:08. Also saw `cudaMalloc` error spikes.

Priya Singh: Customer-facing note: drafting a short status page update. Who will own publishing?

Kate Ops: I can publish once we have a clear mitigation and ETA. Draft below, please edit: "We are investigating increased errors for the Redwood inference API in US-West. Some requests are returning 5xx. Engineers are investigating; no data loss expected. Next update in 30 minutes"

Maya Product: Suggest adding affected endpoints and note "some customers may experience latency/failures". Keep it concise.

Sam (oncall): Mitigation options: 1) revert kernel rollout to previous build (potentially hotspot), 2) drain and restart affected worker pool to clear GPU state, 3) route traffic to us-east-1 fallback pool. Immediate low-risk: scale up worker pool + enable routing to fallback. Revert is medium risk.

Alice Chen: I can trigger a targeted restart of `inf-pool-us-west-2a` and enable fallback routing to us-east-1 for low-priority traffic. Will do controlled restarts of small batches (5 nodes) to avoid mass cold-starts.

Miguel Ramos: Before restart, capture full crash logs + nvml dumps. Alice, can you run `kubectl exec` and collect `/var/log/inference/worker.log` and `nvidia-smi -q` on a failing node?

Alice Chen: Running now. Command output:
```
kubectl exec -it inf-23 -- tail -n 200 /var/log/inference/worker.log
...
E cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
E kv_cache: eviction failed, trying fallback
...
```
And `nvidia-smi -q` shows memory used 98% on GPU0.

Priya Singh: Adding time-aligned timeline notes so far:
- 16:05 — inference-kernel v3.4.2 rollout started (canary)
- 16:20 — rollout reached 40% of us-west pool
- 17:50 — first small spike in 5xxs observed
- 18:08 — sustained error-rate spike, pager triggered
- 18:12 — oncall bridge open

Sam (oncall): That timeline matches. Working hypothesis strengthened: rollout correlated with memory pressure increase.

Liz Eng: Another data point: heavy prefix caching workload ramped up ~17:45 from a single customer (batch job). Prefix KV cache grew 3x. Could be combined effect (more memory used * new kernel alloc behavior = OOM).

Maya Product: If a single customer caused ramp, ops can contact them after mitigation to suggest rate-limiting. Who's owning customer comms?

Priya Singh: I'll own customer outreach for affected customers list. Will draft individualized messages and coord with account execs.

Sam (oncall): Immediate plan: Alice to restart small sets of nodes + enable fallback routing for non-critical traffic. Miguel to monitor memory metrics and nvml logs. Kate to prepare status page draft. Priya to prep customer comms. Liz to watch cache metrics and advise on cache limits throttling.

Alice Chen: Kicking off restart group 1 (nodes inf-21..inf-25). Monitoring.

Miguel Ramos: Observing memory drop after restart on restarted nodes, error-rate partially reduced but still elevated overall.

Sam (oncall): If error-rate doesn't fall to baseline in 10m, we will abort the kernel rollout (rollback to v3.4.1) and force redeploy. Call for 👍/👎.

Liz Eng: 👍 for rollback if it persists. We're seeing cache pressure that likely won't be solved by restarts alone if rollout changes allocation.

Kate Ops: Status page draft v2 (edit ready):
"We are investigating increased 5xx errors for the Redwood inference API in US-West-2. The issue appears related to a recent runtime update interacting with GPU memory usage under heavy cache workloads. Our engineers are performing targeted restarts and enabling fallback routing to reduce customer impact. We will provide updates every 30 minutes or when we have new information. No data loss expected."

Priya Singh: That looks good. I'll prepare customer notes after we confirm mitigation effect.

Alice Chen: Restart group 1 complete. Error-rate dropped from 42% -> 18%. Starting group 2.

Miguel Ramos: After group 2, error-rate is down to 6% and holding. Memory pressure across pool averaged 72% now.

Sam (oncall): Great. For now, keep rollout paused. Action items: Alice — keep controlled restarts for remainder of nodes; Miguel — run full nvml dumps and upload to central logs; Priya — prep customer messages; Kate — publish status page v2 now.

incident-bot: Status update: incident active — mitigation in progress. Next automated check at 1898765499.

Sam (oncall): Closing bridge in 30m if stable. We should capture this timeline into the incident tracker for the post-incident RCA. I'll assign initial owner for RCA: Alice + Miguel.

Alice Chen: I'll start collecting artifact checklist (kernel rollout history, nvml dumps, cache configs, affected node list) and upload to /incidents/1898765432/artifacts.

Priya Singh: Customer impact note: 6 customers briefly impacted; one enterprise had elevated failures — account execs notified.

Liz Eng: Long-term mitigation: add pre-rollout synthetic load test that simulates heavy cache workload, and add guardrails to kernel canary (memory allocation regression detection).

Kate Ops: Status page published. I'll post link here when live.

Maya Product: Thanks team. Keep updates flowing; will prep stakeholder email once we have RCA draft.

Sam (oncall): Thanks all. Will follow up for RCA work and assign next steps.

incident-bot: Incident check: 1898765432 — last update at 1898765499."
